description:
## What

Where does the default pkix-dane-resolver get its upstream DNS server config from?

## Options

- **A) System resolv.conf.** Read /etc/resolv.conf on Unix; equivalent on Windows / macOS. Matches OS DNS behavior. Hickory has built-in support.
- **B) Hardcoded fallback.** Use 1.1.1.1 / 8.8.8.8 / 9.9.9.9. Predictable; corporate-network-unfriendly. Bypasses OS DNS configuration.
- **C) Env variable override + (A) fallback.** `PKIX_DANE_RESOLVER=...` env var; falls back to system config. Maximum operator flexibility.
- **D) Pluggable, no built-in default.** Consumer always provides config. Defeats the 'no consumer code change' goal — but consistent with adapter-trait pattern.

## Considerations

- 'No consumer code change' goal pushes toward (A) or (C).
- Corporate networks often use internal DNS resolvers that handle DNSSEC. (A) respects this.
- DNSSEC-capable system resolvers are common on Linux (systemd-resolved with DNSSEC=allow-downgrade), uncommon on Windows / macOS.
- Some operators specifically want DNSSEC queries to bypass their org's DNS (to avoid filtering). (C) admits this.

## Tentative position

C — env variable override on top of system config. Zero-config behavior matches OS DNS (A); operators get an override knob without code changes; pluggable Resolver trait per non-negotiable #6 lets consumers fully replace if they want.

## Decision-gate

Human-labeled. Surface when PKIX-j32w.2 (pkix-dane-resolver) implementation starts.
title: Decide DNS config source for pkix-dane-resolver
